title: A Multi-Dimensional Framework for Bias Assessment in Indonesia Question-Answering Datasets
venue: JOIV: International Journal on Informatics Visualization
abstract: We aim to develop and validate an Indonesian, fairness-oriented audit for question answering (QA) datasets and to demonstrate its utility on FacQA. Materials comprise ~5,000 question–passage pairs from FacQA and a publicly released IndoBERT-QA checkpoint used without additional fine-tuning. Methodologically, the audit integrates five bias dimensions: (i) topical/entity representation via NER to assess geo-regional and temporal coverage; (ii) question-category imbalance using a 5W+1H scheme; (iii) answer-position effects via a relative-location metric; (iv) length/complexity sensitivity from token-length profiles; and (v) robustness under controlled passage perturbations (front/end relocation, masking, deletion, shuffling). We tokenize with truncation (max length 512) and report EM/F1 with paired significance tests (McNemar for EM; paired bootstrap for F1) across conditions. Results indicate representational skew—GPE dominated by “Indonesia/Jakarta” and dates largely pre-2005—and structural imbalance—“What/How many” far outnumber other types, with no “Why/How.” Answers concentrate early in passages (41.45% early; 32.63% middle; 25.92% late) and are short (≥70% have 1–3 tokens). Perturbations show a small, non-significant early-position advantage (Δ≈1.2 pp EM), consistent with lead bias in the sources. Implications for practice include curating more balanced Indonesian QA resources (diversifying time periods and regions, adding “Why/How,” and documenting length-/position-stratified coverage) and standardizing evaluations that report Original vs. front/end variants with robustness checks and paired testing. For further research, we outline extending probes to Indonesian social-bias axes, evaluating zero-/few-shot LLMs under the same audit, and auditing retrieval choices in RAG pipelines to mitigate corpus-induced skew.
